title: UI hang due to bad messages injected from dumpcap
description:
* Some libraries may write error messages to the stderr.
    These messages will pollute the messages in sync pipe
    of dumpcap. In this case the wireshark will be confusing
    about these messages. This commit demostrate this issue.

notes.body:
> This commit demostrate this issue.

By "demonstrate[s]" do you mean "fixes" or "tries to catch the problem and report it without hanging"?  (I'd say a commit "demonstrates" the issue by deliberately making dumpcap write out a plain-text error message to stderr, so as to cause the problem to happen.)

Hi Guy,

this commit can be regarded as an ugly "fixes" to the issue if we really have no better idea. This not only demonstrates how the error messages mixed in the dumpcap output can affect wireshark, but also provides a potential way to make wireshark quit executation whitout hanging when encountering such situations.

The provided link [libibverbs issue](https://github.com/lonicerae/rdma-core/commit/d6680a045e9183175fbf12afdec4c369d2d6ab0d) is intentionally created as a reproduction with the purpose of making errors more observable. In actuality, the library `libibverbs.so` does throw error messages to the standard error due to various conditions, causing wireshark to become unresponsive. Due to confidential reason, I could not show the orignal strace sample for you.

However, through careful analysis, I have confirmed that the following message is mixed into the standard error of dumpcap when dumpcap loads pcap and then pcap loads other libraries.

`libi40iw-i40iw_ucreate_qp: failed to create QP, unsupported QP type: 0x8`

Therefore, it's necessary for wireshark to:
1. Validate the output from dupmcap, or
2. To require dumpcap to properly distinguish interference messages from its loaded libraries.

In fact, you can try using my [libibverbs issue](https://github.com/lonicerae/rdma-core/commit/d6680a045e9183175fbf12afdec4c369d2d6ab0d) with all existing official wireshark versions. They'll hang forever when they try to find interfaces.

Feel free to let me know if you have any thoughts about this. Thanks.

Best regards,
Flos

> Validate the output from dupmcap

That would probably be difficult to do in the general case.

> To require dumpcap to properly distinguish interference messages from its loaded libraries.

That would be the ideal.  It would mean sending dumpcap's stderr down a separate pipe from any control and data pipes, and having the program that runs dumpcap - or the shared code used by those programs - read from that pipe, store the messages away, and show them if there's an error reported.

I'm not sure how easy it is to do that on Windows.

> That would probably be difficult to do in the general case.

Like what I try at https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/11311/diffs#cd122886d3fe4d4d4dc93808b4735110c63ce597_1563_1572 , but I also think it's hard to implement because we don't know when bad messages will be injected into the stderr, maybe it's possible mixing with normal data..

> That would be the ideal.

Yep, that would be a good solution.
